title: A text statistics tool
description:
Read a sentence and report on its words.

```
Text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
Words: 9
Letters: 35
Longest word: quick
Words starting with a capital: 1
```

starter.main.py:
text = input("Text: ")
words = text.split()

# TODO: count the letters, find the longest word, count capitalised words

print(f"Words: {len(words)}")

hints: Loop over each word, and inside that over each character, adding 1 when `ch.isalpha()`.
Keep `longest = ""` and replace it only when `len(word) > len(longest)`: with `>` and not `>=`, the first of two equal words stays.
requirements: Split the text into words with `split()`.
Count only letters (`isalpha`) for the letter count.
If two words are equally long, the first one wins.
stretch: Print how many times each letter appears, most common first (milestone 5 shows a shorter way).
